name: Solder Sunday
description: An informal weekly-turned-annual mega-observance held the first Sunday of November, celebrating the Shelf tradition of hardware salvage, DIY augmentation, and unauthorized tech modification. What began in 2191 as a recurring swap meet under the Lakeward Viaduct has grown into a sprawling, semi-nomadic festival culture, with ghost markets, open-air repair clinics, and competitive 'chrome-offs' where amateur cyberware builders demonstrate functional augmentations built entirely from salvage. The festival's defining ritual is the Solder Kiss — touching the tip of a heated soldering iron to your own palm scar to prove you built something with your hands this year.
cultural_impact: Solder Sunday has made DIY augmentation culturally visible and given Shelf tech workers a rare moment of public pride; it has also become the primary annual distribution point for unauthorized medical-grade chrome in Tier 1, saving lives that licensed augmentation clinics price out of reach. Corporate augmentation brands quietly monitor the event for IP violations while also poaching the most talented builders they identify.
key_figures: Patch (E.L.F. event coordinator and parts directory)
locations: The Bone Pit Salvage Yard, South Corridor
Rotating ghost market sites announced 48 hours prior
story_hooks: This year's Solder Sunday ghost market location has been leaked to corporate security — someone inside the organizing collective is selling information, and the community needs to know who before the sweep happens.
A chrome-off competitor shows up with an augmentation that shouldn't exist — military-grade hardware with no manufacturing marks — and has no memory of building it.
Nneka Vasquez-Huang, the aging founder, announces this will be her last Solder Sunday — and that she's leaving the event's organizational keys to an E.L.F., which has fractured the community.
origin_event: In 2191, Nneka Vasquez-Huang organized a recurring Sunday hardware swap under the Lakeward Viaduct after the closure of the last licensed repair shop in Ward 7, giving Shelf residents their only access to augmentation maintenance. The November mega-event emerged organically by 2197 as the year's largest gathering.
tier_observations: Tier 1: Full participation — vendors, builders, repair clinics, chrome-offs, the Solder Kiss ritual; it is a genuine community celebration. Tier 2: Many attend as customers or spectators; some participate in repair clinics; the Solder Kiss is observed by those with Shelf roots. Tier 3: A small number visit for the aesthetic and the finds; largely treated as slumming tourism, which causes real tension with locals. Tier 4-5: Unaware or dismissive; corporate augmentation brands send plainclothes monitors.
